result.worker_process: separate Node/tsx process; actual runWorkerLoop and EncodeJobRepository claim
result.pipeline: real six-second synthetic MP4; FFmpeg 8.0.1; OriginalsReader/HlsWriter with AWS SDK; HLS verification; Prisma finalizer and PostgreSQL route/asset/job writes
result.object_storage: in-memory S3-shaped loopback HTTP fixture; 127.0.0.1 only

assertions: Only the requested queued job was eligible before the worker ran.
The job reached SUCCEEDED/DONE at 100 percent with a generated attemptId.
The database has exactly one active route and one READY SELF_HLS asset for the fixture video.
The asset key is scoped to the generated attemptId.
The loopback store contains master and variant playlists, an fMP4 segment, and poster; HlsWriter verified playlist references before finalization.
limitations: Does not call Next.js upload or playback HTTP routes and is not a browser test.
The helper assembles production worker-loop components but does not launch scripts/video-worker.ts itself.
The loopback S3-shaped fixture is not Cloudflare R2 and proves no provider semantics, durability, ETag/CORS, or edge playback.
K01-T3 and K35 remain partial; real R2 acceptance and independent review remain open.
